summary: Firebase Wave 1 is complete and correct against requirements.md (AC-1..AC-31) and design.md Revision 4. I independently ran `npx tsc --noEmit` (0 errors) and `npx expo lint` (0 errors, 1 pre-existing react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warning in the untouched src/screens/DiscoverScreen.tsx — not introduced by this wave). Every whole-wave invariant holds: no file in src/screens/*.tsx imports firebase or the pickers (verified by search); only config.ts calls initializeApp/initializeAuth/getFirestore/getStorage and there is no getAnalytics anywhere; Auth is initialized over AsyncStorage via a hand-written Persistence adapter (design.md step-3 fallback, correctly taken because `@firebase/auth` getReactNativePersistence does not resolve under the project tsconfig); partner is blocked inside AccountContext.signUp with the app/partner-not-available sentinel BEFORE any Firebase call, so no auth user, no session and no users/{uid} profile is ever created for a partner; RootNavigator in _layout.tsx is the sole redirect owner (both wrappers only set local submitting/errorMessage and never navigate) and gates the splash on fontsReady && !loading with setLoading(false) in a finally so the gate can never hang; favorites persist per-user with optimistic per-id rollback and a null-guard, reviews read/write businesses/{businessId}/reviews with avgRating guarded against the empty list and null createdAt never dereferenced, tasks seed idempotently with fixed ids t1/t2 and persist done with the irreversible UX preserved, and documents upload/list/delete via Storage under users/{uid}/documents with a pure screen + hook. FloatingNav, the discover-data catalog seed, and the 'terracota' literal in constants.ts are all untouched (empty git diff). The only residual items are runtime-only facts that a green tsc/lint cannot prove and that design.md explicitly defers to a manual Expo Go smoke test (Firebase credentials and the storageBucket string); these are documented NITs, not code defects, so they are not blocking.

findings.detail: The committed storageBucket default uses the newer 'gen-lang-client-0201344960.firebasestorage.app' form and the apiKey/messagingSenderId/appId are committed literals. A green tsc/lint does not prove these are the correct console values — a wrong bucket fails silently (init succeeds; the first uploadBytes/listAll fails at runtime). Before shipping, smoke-test one real signup/login (session survives app reload) and one real document upload+list in Expo Go, as design.md's MUST-fill/storageBucket notes require. No code change needed; this is a manual verification step outside tsc/lint reach.

The missing-profile edge case sets an internal one-time profileError string that is intentionally not part of the public context value, so no screen currently surfaces 'Não foi possível carregar seu perfil. Entre novamente.' (the destructured setter uses an unused first slot `const [, setProfileError]`). This matches the design's stated decision to keep it internal for Wave 1; if a later wave wants to show it, promote it into the context value. Not blocking.
